messages:
Maria L.: Heads up — CI perf suite for release/v1.12.0 showed a significant regression on the runtime p99 (about +12%). failing job: https://ci.internal/redwood/12345 :frowning:
perf-bot: [CI] perf/regression job 12345 failed (p99 +12%). Logs uploaded: https://ci.internal/artifacts/12345/perf.zip
Jon T.: thanks. can someone try a quick git bisect between the v1.11 tag and HEAD of release/v1.12? my hunch: kernel-selection refactor or batching heuristics tweak.
Kai P.: I'll start a local bisect. quick notes for repro command I use locally:
```
# warm VM with same kernels
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=auto
export REDWOOD_CACHE_POLICY=conservative
./tools/bench/serve_bench --model=redwood/llama-13b --seq=1024 --batch=4 --iters=200 --profile > out.txt
```
Kai P.: on a first pass I can reproduce ~10% p99 increase when I pick the post-merge tree. attaching a small profile excerpt: 
```
[profile] kernel_selected=fused-attn-v2 -> generic-attn
[profile] avg_token_time 0.83ms -> 0.94ms
[profile] kv_cache_hits 98% -> 87%
```
Olivia R.: that kernel switch stands out — we recently changed the kernel scoring to prefer memory-safe fallback for long sequences (PR cdef456). could be the regression.
Dmitri S.: do we have a quick perf-bisect script? i can run `git bisect run` with the bench if we have a deterministic script.
Jon T.: create a tiny runner that exits nonzero when p99 exceeds baseline + 5%. example: `./tools/bisect/run_perf_check.sh`. command: 
```
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v1.11.0
git bisect run ./tools/bisect/run_perf_check.sh
```
Maria L.: Kai, can you start the bisect run on the larger machine? tag me if it ends up pointing to a single commit so we can decide revert vs patch.
Kai P.: running now. ETA ~25 mins. sending updates.
perf-bot: bisect job started by Kai P. runner: bisect-runner-35. logs: https://ci.internal/artifacts/bisect/1769910200/
Kai P.: quick discovery: the bisect run keeps flipping around commits that touch `batching/heuristics.go` and `kernelselect/score.go`. when pinned to pre-cdef456 kernel selection we see baseline numbers. git says the culprit is in the window: ab12f3..cdef456
Olivia R.: I looked at cdef456 — it introduced a conservative tie-breaker that demotes fused kernels for sequences > 512 if memory estimate > threshold. probably too aggressive.
Dmitri S.: is there any difference in KV cache policy? the profile earlier showed kv cache hit drop — maybe the new batching heuristics ended up fragmenting KV cache usage.
Jon T.: good catch. try forcing KV cache policy back to aggressive and re-run bench on the suspect commit to see if p99 recovers. env: `REDWOOD_CACHE_POLICY=aggressive`
Kai P.: tried that. partial recover but still ~4% worse. so kernel choice is majority factor.
Maria L.: action: open a revert PR for cdef456 as rollback-candidate. Jon, can you create the PR and tag eng-runtime + SRE for canary?
Jon T.: will do. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/repo/pull/893 (revert cdef456). I'll add a canary rollout plan: 10% traffic on dedicated pool -> monitor p99, token cost, OOMs for 1h.
Olivia R.: also add a follow-up to rework the kernel scoring to consider actual runtime sampling (not just mem estimate). add a perf test in CI that asserts kernel selection stability for long-seq workloads.
Dmitri S.: after revert lands, i'll run end-to-end KV cache sweep tests to ensure we didn't mask a separate KV regression.
Maria L.: thanks everyone. Kai — please paste the final bisect output here when complete. once PR is up i'll trigger the canary. :thumbsup:
Kai P.: final bisect result: `cdef456 is the first bad commit` — shortlog: "kernelselect: conservative tie-breaker for long sequences". full output: https://ci.internal/artifacts/bisect/1769910200/result.txt
Jon T.: PR created and link posted. asking for expedited review. reverting now is safest given customer SLAs.
perf-bot: Canary deployment started for PR #893 -> dedicated-pool-canary-7. watch: https://console.redwood/inflight/canaries/7
Maria L.: closing the loop — thanks team. after canary completes we'll decide whether to backport to v1.12 and add the CI kernel-selection stability test.
Olivia R.: follow-up tickets: PERF-412 (kernel scoring revamp), PERF-413 (CI kernel selection check), PERF-414 (kv-cache regression audit).
Dmitri S.: noted. I'll pick up PERF-414 tomorrow.
Jon T.: merging revert on green.
Maria L.: :tada:
